flows.narrative: Re-confirmed this run (Thu 26 Nov, Thanksgiving): no newer BofA/EPFR or Lipper edition has published since the week-ended-18-Nov figures first appeared three runs ago. A Nov-22-dated Hartnett Flow Show commentary piece ('Johnny Lovedrop to Billy Big Boots') was found and checked -- it discusses the same week-ended-18-Nov data window, not a new data week, so it does not change anything here. Underlying figures remain: global equity funds +$59.23bn Lipper / +$66.6bn BofA, 9th straight week; US equities +$45.71bn, largest since 23 Sep; tech funds +$12.3bn Lipper; Bull & Bear Indicator at 7.1, down from 7.4, driven by EM-debt and high-yield outflows and wider credit spreads. EM debt saw -$7.5bn outflows (most since April 2020) even as EM equities kept drawing +$1.98-8.3bn inflows -- a debt/equity divergence; Europe gained +$1.5bn (most since Feb) while Japan lost -$4.2bn (biggest since May). This window (through Wed 18 Nov) still predates the Nov 20 crash, Nov 23 Nvidia-driven rebound, and the Nov 24-25 consolidation entirely -- whenever the week-ending-25-Nov edition finally publishes, it will be the first to show any reaction, covering the full round trip plus the subsequent two-session wobble. Separately, prime-brokerage data (Goldman, via Tickmill) previously showed hedge funds stayed net sellers of US equities into Monday's rally and that the +4.73% S&P bounce was short-covering (a ~$19bn forced cover after selling ~$57bn over the prior month, Goldman desk conviction only 5/10) rather than fresh institutional buying, while retail (Vanda) kept buying dips, net +$3.49bn into Nvidia alone from Nov 4-23 -- no update to that prime-brokerage read was found this run.
